chunks: 13 — What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام: that he was asked about tayammum with gypsum, and he said:
"Yes." Then it was said: with lime? He said: "Yes." Then it was said: with ashes? He said: "No. It does not come out of the earth; rather, it only comes out of trees."

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, the dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.الرَّمَادِ: ashes, ruled invalid here for tayammum
key_terms.الشَّجَرِ: trees, the source of ashes and the reason given for their invalidity in tayammum
key_terms.النُّورَةِ: lime, another earth-derived substance permitted for tayammum in this report
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth, the criterion for what qualifies as valid material for tayammum
key_terms.الْجِصِّ: gypsum, a material with which tayammum is affirmed as valid here

ai.seo_question: Is tayammum valid with gypsum, lime, or ashes in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding tayammum and the materials with which it may be performed. It permits tayammum with gypsum and lime, but not with ashes, because ashes are not regarded as coming from the earth; rather, they come from trees.
